issues.check: customer kg exceeds laundry total kg
issues.location: L003: 12 month(s), customer kg = 9.6–12.6× the laundry's total
issues.explanation: For 12 laundry-month(s) customers' washed kg is larger than the laundry's own washed kg (L003: 12 month(s), customer kg = 9.6–12.6× the laundry's total). A share above 100 % is impossible, so one of the two volumes is wrong (a unit slip of ~10× is typical). Allocated metrics use per-kg intensities, which do not depend on these absolute volumes, but the laundry figures should be verified.
issues.fix: Verify the laundry washed_kg (and units) for the listed laundries with the data owner. Metrics are kept by default.

metrics.label: Delivery sites
metrics.formula: count of distinct site_id in service activity

metrics.label: Textiles washed
metrics.formula: sum of customer_washed_kg

metrics.label: Active wearers (2025-12, may double-count)
metrics.formula: sum of active_wearers over product rows in the last month

metrics.label: Garments allocated (2025-12)
metrics.formula: sum of allocated_pieces in the last month

metrics.label: Service requests
metrics.formula: sum of service_requests

metrics.label: Garment utilisation (garments with scan activity ÷ allocated)
metrics.formula: Σ active_assets_scanned ÷ Σ allocated_pieces in the last month
metrics.note: Allocated garments with no scan activity are an investigation signal, not a conclusion: they may not have needed washing, may not yet be picked up, or scan data may be incomplete.

metrics.label: Water intensity (Lindström)
metrics.formula: Σ(kg × laundry L/kg) ÷ Σ kg × allocation factor

metrics.label: Water saved vs Outsourced local laundry
metrics.formula: Σ matched kg × baseline L/kg × baseline factor − Σ matched kg × laundry L/kg × allocation factor
metrics.note: Laundry water is allocated to the customer by washed kg (assumption X01).

metrics.label: Energy intensity (Lindström)
metrics.formula: Σ(kg × laundry kWh/kg) ÷ Σ kg × allocation factor

metrics.label: Energy saved vs Outsourced local laundry
metrics.formula: Σ matched kg × baseline kWh/kg × baseline factor − Σ matched kg × laundry kWh/kg × allocation factor

metrics.label: Service emissions saved vs Outsourced local laundry
metrics.formula: Σ matched kg × baseline (process+delivery kgCO2e/kg) × baseline factor − Σ matched kg × laundry (process+delivery kgCO2e/kg) × allocation factor

metrics.label: Textile waste attributed
metrics.formula: Σ kg × laundry textile waste per washed kg × allocation factor

metrics.label: Textile waste recycled or reused
metrics.formula: Σ(kg × waste/kg × (recycling+reuse share)) ÷ Σ(kg × waste/kg)
metrics.note: Laundry-level treatment routes allocated by washed kg.

metrics.label: Repairs completed
metrics.formula: sum of repair_count

metrics.label: Replacements postponed
metrics.formula: repairs × replacements-postponed factor
metrics.note: Pack assumption A002: 1 completed repair postpones 1 replacement. Low case 0.5.

metrics.label: Purchases avoided, upper-bound estimate
metrics.formula: Σ repair_count × product purchase cost × repair factor
metrics.note: Direct avoided purchase only; no labour or lifetime effects (assumption X05).

metrics.label: Avoided product emissions
metrics.formula: Σ repair_count × product footprint (or stated avoided kgCO2e) × repair factor
metrics.note: Product footprints are illustrative, not approved LCA values.

metrics.label: On-time service cycles
metrics.formula: share of service cycles with performance_flag = ON_TIME

metrics.label: Avg. cycle time (pickup→delivery)
metrics.formula: mean cycle_hours (or delivered − pickup timestamp)

opportunities.title: Agree the right comparison baseline and make the resource story reportable
opportunities.hypothesis: The water and energy saving depends heavily on what the customer would otherwise use. Agreeing the baseline turns an estimate into evidence the customer can use in its own reporting.
opportunities.sizing: 1.41 M L of water and 171.6 k kWh of energy versus the selected baseline.
evidence: Allocated water use 6.7 L/kg vs baseline; saving 1.41 M L (range 116.2 k L to 2.70 M L).
The saving holds for any alternative that uses more than 6.7 L/kg.
assumptions: Baseline intensities are illustrative pack values.
Laundry use is allocated by washed kg.
confirm: What would you use otherwise: local laundry, in-house, home washing?
Do you have your own litres/kg or kWh/kg?

opportunities.title: Agree a service-continuity plan for the sites that stand out
opportunities.hypothesis: A few sites show more service requests or weaker on-time delivery than the rest. A joint root-cause review could improve reliability where it matters most.
opportunities.sizing: 2 site(s); 35 service requests at these sites in the period.
evidence: 2 of 24 sites stand out against this customer's other sites: NorthStar Gdańsk (requests 63 per 1000 vs median 15; on-time 97.8 %); NorthStar Tampere (requests 57 per 1000 vs median 15; on-time 98.3 %).
assumptions: Flag = robust outlier vs this customer's own sites with a minimum effect size; a signal, not a diagnosis.
confirm: What happened at these sites (contacts, layout, delivery windows)?
Are the requests about the same cause?

opportunities.title: Provide Scope 3 evidence the customer can use
opportunities.hypothesis: Customers increasingly ask for customer-specific footprint evidence. An agreed method and data status would let them use these figures in reporting.
opportunities.sizing: 255.1 k kgCO2e service emissions saving (allocated estimate).
evidence: Service emissions 255.1 k kgCO2e lower than the selected baseline (range 181.9 k kgCO2e to 328.2 k kgCO2e). Avoided product emissions through repair: 224.3 k kgCO2e (estimate).
assumptions: Synthetic factors and allocation by washed kg.
Repair handprint assumes 1 repair postpones 1 replacement (upper bound).
confirm: Which reporting framework do you use?
What data status do you need (measured vs allocated)?
opportunities.caveat: Not usable as an audited figure until approved factors and measured allocation replace the synthetic data.

opportunities.title: Set a hygiene-control threshold using garment scan data
opportunities.hypothesis: Scan data can show garments that have not been through the wash cycle for a long time. With a threshold agreed per customer, this becomes a garment-control routine.
opportunities.sizing: 1427 garments at 90 days (threshold editable); top sites: NorthStar Västerås (74), NorthStar Seinäjoki (74), NorthStar Uppsala (71)
evidence: 2127 garments with scans; median time since last delivery 134 days (90th percentile 247).
At a 90-day threshold, 1427 garments (67 %) would be flagged as of 2026-01-04.
assumptions: The 90-day threshold is illustrative; the customer defines what is acceptable.
Sample cycles are sparse (3-8 per garment per year), so results are indicative.
confirm: Which threshold fits your hygiene plan?
Who acts on a flag, and how fast?
opportunities.caveat: RFID is per garment; shown at site/group level only, never named wearers (GDPR).

opportunities.title: Review garment allocation per site
opportunities.hypothesis: Some allocated garments are not in active use. A site-by-site review could match allocation to real use and improve garment control.
opportunities.sizing: ≈ 5 230 garments not scanned in the last month (16 % of allocation); a buffer stock is normal, its size is the customer's to define.
evidence: Garment utilisation 83.5 % (scanned ÷ allocated, last month).
About 5 230 of 31 743 allocated garments were not scanned; the 3 lowest sites (NorthStar Kotka, NorthStar Helsinki, NorthStar Łódź) hold 17 % of them.
assumptions: Scanned = in use during the month.
Seasonality and buffer policy are not in the data.
confirm: What buffer level does each site need?
Are there seasonal or shift-based peaks?
opportunities.caveat: A smaller allocation can reduce rental volume. Frame it as retention and trust, not as a sales lever.

opportunities.title: Review repair-heavy products for durability
opportunities.hypothesis: Products with a high repair rate may benefit from a durability or fit review, which reduces repairs and extends garment life.
opportunities.sizing: 5816 repairs on Work Jacket Standard; 15 233 replacements postponed at the selected assumption (range 7 616 to 15 233).
evidence: 15.2 k repairs completed. Highest repair rate: Work Jacket Standard at 0.57 repairs per allocated garment per year (all products: 0.48).
assumptions: 1 repair postpones 1 replacement is an upper bound (Low case 0.5).
Repair rate = repairs ÷ mean allocated garments.
confirm: Do wearers report fit or wear problems with this product?
Is the damage type consistent (button, zip, seam)?
opportunities.caveat: Rates across products are similar in the sample data; treat as a prompt for discussion, not a finding.

recommendations.title: Make the resource story explicit
recommendations.text: Allocated water use is 6.7 L/kg against Outsourced local laundry; 1.41 M L saved in the period (range 116.2 k L to 2.70 M L). The result is sensitive to the baseline; agree with the customer which baseline fits their situation before using it in sustainability reporting.
recommendations.basis: water saving = washed kg × baseline L/kg − allocated water (ALLOCATED; range from baseline and allocation sensitivity)

recommendations.title: Agree an action plan for flagged sites
recommendations.text: 2 of 24 sites combine at least two weak signals (low garment utilisation, late cycles, high service-request rate), e.g. NorthStar Tampere, NorthStar Gdańsk. By country: {'Finland': 1, 'Poland': 1}. Ask the site managers what is behind it.
recommendations.basis: Relative rule: robust outlier vs the customer's own sites (median/MAD) on ≥2 indicators, or extreme on one

recommendations.title: Clarify garment sharing and traceability
recommendations.text: 6 site(s) report more active wearers than allocated garments (NorthStar Turku, NorthStar Tampere, NorthStar Lahti). Garments are probably shared. Agree how wearer counts should be defined, and keep reporting at site/group level, never named individuals.
recommendations.basis: wearers > allocated pieces (data gap, GDPR-safe aggregation)

recommendations.title: Right-size the garment allocation
recommendations.text: Garment utilisation is 83.5 %. Lowest sites: NorthStar Kotka, NorthStar Helsinki, NorthStar Łódź (76-79 %). About 5 230 allocated garments were not scanned in the last month: review allocation or wearer-to-garment ratios before next year's order.
recommendations.basis: utilisation = scanned ÷ allocated (CALCULATED)

recommendations.title: Extend garment life with repair
recommendations.text: 15.2 k repairs completed; at the selected assumption that postpones 15.2 k pieces and avoids about 660.1 k EUR of purchases (range 330.0 k EUR to 660.1 k EUR). Discuss repair-heavy products and whether damage prevention could cut repairs further.
recommendations.basis: postponed = repairs × factor (ESTIMATED, sensitivity-tested)

recommendations.title: Provide Scope 3 evidence
recommendations.text: Service emissions are 255.1 k kgCO2e lower than Outsourced local laundry, plus 224.3 k kgCO2e of avoided product emissions (estimate). Agree which of these the customer may use in its own reporting once real data replaces synthetic factors.
recommendations.basis: ALLOCATED + ESTIMATED; status shown per number

recommendations.title: Agree data fixes that would firm up next year's review
recommendations.text: 1 error(s) and 3 warning(s) were found in the data, e.g. customer kg exceeds laundry total kg; no status label. Assign owners for the fixes before the next review.
recommendations.basis: validation report (all issues listed in the app and the deck)

opportunities.sizing: 18.7 k kgCO2e service emissions saving (allocated estimate).
evidence: Service emissions 18.7 k kgCO2e lower than the selected baseline (range 8 427 kgCO2e to 28.9 k kgCO2e). Avoided product emissions through repair: 21.9 k kgCO2e (estimate).
assumptions: Synthetic factors and allocation by washed kg.
Repair handprint assumes 1 repair postpones 1 replacement (upper bound).
confirm: Which reporting framework do you use?
What data status do you need (measured vs allocated)?
opportunities.caveat: Not usable as an audited figure until approved factors and measured allocation replace the synthetic data.

recommendations.title: Agree an action plan for flagged sites
recommendations.text: 1 of 4 sites combine at least two weak signals (low garment utilisation, late cycles, high service-request rate), e.g. Mediora Kraków. By country: {'Poland': 1}. Ask the site managers what is behind it.
recommendations.basis: Relative rule: robust outlier vs the customer's own sites (median/MAD) on ≥2 indicators, or extreme on one

recommendations.title: Right-size the garment allocation
recommendations.text: Garment utilisation is 85.9 %. Lowest sites: Mediora Kraków, Mediora Poznań, Mediora Warsaw (81-89 %). About 759 allocated garments were not scanned in the last month: review allocation or wearer-to-garment ratios before next year's order.
recommendations.basis: utilisation = scanned ÷ allocated (CALCULATED)

recommendations.title: Make the resource story explicit
recommendations.text: Allocated water use is 6.9 L/kg against Outsourced local laundry; 161.5 k L saved in the period (range 2 253 L to 320.8 k L). The result is sensitive to the baseline; agree with the customer which baseline fits their situation before using it in sustainability reporting.
recommendations.basis: water saving = washed kg × baseline L/kg − allocated water (ALLOCATED; range from baseline and allocation sensitivity)

recommendations.title: Extend garment life with repair
recommendations.text: 1929 repairs completed; at the selected assumption that postpones 1929 pieces and avoids about 67.4 k EUR of purchases (range 33.7 k EUR to 67.4 k EUR). Discuss repair-heavy products and whether damage prevention could cut repairs further.
recommendations.basis: postponed = repairs × factor (ESTIMATED, sensitivity-tested)

recommendations.title: Provide Scope 3 evidence
recommendations.text: Service emissions are 18.7 k kgCO2e lower than Outsourced local laundry, plus 21.9 k kgCO2e of avoided product emissions (estimate). Agree which of these the customer may use in its own reporting once real data replaces synthetic factors.
recommendations.basis: ALLOCATED + ESTIMATED; status shown per number

recommendations.title: Agree data fixes that would firm up next year's review
recommendations.text: 1 error(s) and 3 warning(s) were found in the data, e.g. customer kg exceeds laundry total kg; no status label. Assign owners for the fixes before the next review.
recommendations.basis: validation report (all issues listed in the app and the deck)

CUST003.narrative: In the review period Mediora Health Network had 61.6 k kg of textiles washed across 4 sites. With the focus on **service**: 98.4 % of service cycles were on time at 82.3 h average turnaround, with 62 requests. Next: agree an action plan for flagged sites.
